summary: An operator asked how to rebuild the images and bring the homepage up on the central PC. Measuring the answer showed the deployment docs would produce the wrong stack. Three defects, all of the same family: prose that was true when written and was never re-derived. (1) infra/central/ONPREM_DEPLOYMENT.md tells you to cd into the provider repository at four places. That file was last touched by the extraction delivery commit and never updated for the 2026-09-03 placement change, while the gated runbook says the central PC holds this repository and not the provider one. The two repositories each carry an infra/docker-compose.central.yml and they differ: the provider copy defines six services with no build stanza for web, this one defines seven including platform-api-node. So following the deployment doc verbatim brings up a stack without the instance that splits browser and node auth, and cannot build the web image. infra/central/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md has the same cd. (2) Three operational docs print an expected container list that predates platform-api-node, so an operator who counts them concludes the stack is broken when it is healthy. (3) ONPREM_DEPLOYMENT.md corrects python to python3 in section 5 and then commits that same mistake in the verification section of the same file. Separately, the operational-validation runbook verifies PUBLIC_HOST with hostname -I, which on this WSL setup lists nine addresses of which the Windows host actually owns one; the other eight pass a check the runbook itself warns will bounce the login. FOURTH ITEM, added while the operator was running the deployment live: the stack stopped at central-migrate with exit 3, a checksum drift on 001, which left platform-api, platform-api-node and web down because they gate on that job completing. The root cause is a category error. 001 is a generated artifact - its own first line says "Generated from docs/platform/central_db_schema.v1.json" - and it sits inside an append-only checksummed ledger. On an existing database 001 is never re-applied, only compared, and that comparison cannot in principle distinguish "the exporter regenerated it" from "a person edited it": both read as different. So the comparison had no true positive available to it, and its only effect was to stop every deployment that followed a legitimate schema change, with an error message that accused someone of an edit nobody made. The check that CAN discriminate already existed elsewhere and is stronger than a checksum: TestChamberSchemaDdlDrift re-renders the DDL from the schema JSON and requires byte equality. So the generated bootstrap leaves the ledger drift axis, derived from the file header rather than a hardcoded name, and a new seal asserts the replacement check still exists so that removing it reopens the hole loudly instead of silently. Proven by injection: hand-editing 001 is still caught.
non_scope: The provider repository's copy of infra/docker-compose.central.yml. It is the other lane's file and the monorepo CI is left alone by operator decision (2026-09-07).
Fixing the central PC itself. This claim changes documents and a seal; whether the deployment is re-run is the operator's call and container start is an approval point.
The chamber PC cd sites in central-pc-update-deploy-runbook.md and the operational-validation runbook. Those name the provider repository correctly - the chamber PC is where it belongs.
